rubric.how: Award 1 mark for CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl, allowing equivalent notation.

items.followUp: State two differences between the Bohr model and the modern atomic model.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy specific allowed orbits around the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that electrons move in fixed, permitted circular orbits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the allowed circular orbits or energy levels.

rubric.why: An electron in a stationary orbit does not lose energy by radiation.
rubric.description: States that an electron does not radiate energy while in an allowed orbit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the no-radiation postulate.

rubric.why: The quantization condition specifies which electron orbits are allowed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mvr = nh/2pi or an equivalent expression.

rubric.why: Energy is absorbed or emitted when an electron changes its energy level.
rubric.description: States the rule for absorption or emission during a transition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing an electron jump accompanied by absorption or emission of energy.

rubric.why: The allowed energy states are separate rather than continuous.
rubric.description: States that energy levels are discrete and there are no intermediate allowed energies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the discrete nature of the energy levels.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed, permitted circular orbits called stationary orbits or energy levels.
Each permitted orbit has a definite energy, and an electron does not radiate energy while it remains in that orbit.
The angular momentum of an electron in an allowed orbit is quantized: mvr = nh/2pi, where n = 1, 2, 3, ...
An electron absorbs or emits energy only when it jumps between energy levels; the energy change is ΔE = hν.
The energy levels are discrete, so electrons cannot have energies between the permitted levels.

items.followUp: Define a mixture and name its two main types.

rubric.why: A compound is formed by chemical combination and has a fixed composition.
rubric.description: Defines a compound as elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the definition includes elements, chemical combination and a fixed proportion.

rubric.why: Organic compounds form one class in the composition-based classification.
rubric.description: Names organic compounds and identifies them as carbon compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming organic compounds and describing them as carbon compounds.

rubric.why: Inorganic compounds form the other class in this classification.
rubric.description: Names inorganic compounds and gives an example or suitable description.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inorganic compounds and giving sodium chloride as an example.

rubric.why: Compounds may also be classified according to their type of bonding.
rubric.description: Gives a correct bonding-based class with an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for ionic NaCl or molecular/covalent H2O.

modelAnswer: A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more elements chemically combine in a fixed proportion.
By composition, compounds are classified as organic and inorganic. Organic compounds are carbon compounds, while inorganic compounds include substances such as sodium chloride and water.
By the type of bonding, compounds may also be classified as ionic, such as NaCl, or molecular (covalent), such as H2O.

items.followUp: What is an ion? Distinguish between a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: An ion is an atom or group of atoms with a net charge, usually due to electron gain or loss.
rubric.description: Defines an ion as an atom or group of atoms carrying a net electric charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that identifies the charged atom or group.

rubric.why: Cations and anions are the two types of ions, distinguished by charge sign.
rubric.description: Names cations as positive ions and anions as negative ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types and giving their correct charges.

modelAnswer: An ion is an atom or group of atoms carrying a net electric charge because it has gained or lost electrons.
Its types are cations, which are positively charged, and anions, which are negatively charged.

rubric.why: The mass divided by the molar mass gives half a mole of water.
rubric.description: Gives the correct number of moles with its unit.
